text:
Alex M.: Heads up — prod inference clusters are showing a "memory cascade" on the KV cache after the awq-int8 kernel rollout last night. Paging events spiked across three nodes, latency SLOs degraded for a subset of heavy chat routes. Link to graph: https://grafana.internal/d/PROD/kv-cache

Maria P.: seeing the same. Which rollout exactly? awq-int8-v2? :eyes:

Alex M.: yes awq-int8-v2 rolled @ 03:12 UTC yesterday. The cluster-level metric shows KV_TOTAL_BYTES jumped ~3.8x on int8 paths for long-prefix workloads, eviction count exploded.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT OPENED — INC-3789 — KV cache paging surge detected (alert: kv_cache_paging_rate > 30m avg). Pager: @Jamal R.

Elaine S.: quick triage: logs show this pattern: kernel selected awq-int8 for many models; AWQ's per-kv-element packing seems to expand in our runtime (likely alignment/padding + kernel metadata). Example log snippet:
```
[WARN] kv_cache.cpp: eviction spike, recent_evictions=1320, window=30s
[WARN] kernel_selector.cpp: selected=awq-int8-v2, estimated_kv_bytes=7800000000
[INFO] batcher.cpp: continuous_batching=true, avg_batch_tokens=450
```
This matches a continuous batching config that keeps larger KV caches hot.

Maria P.: customer impact? Which tenants/routes are affected?

Alex M.: early list: chat-heavy tenants (ids t-42, t-108), and some long-context embeddings workloads. We'll need to unblock traffic quickly.

Elaine S.: mitigation plan (live):
1) disable continuous batching globally for the affected pools
2) force kernel fallback to fp16 path or older int8 implementation for the hot models
3) apply temporary eviction-throttle (lower in-memory kv limit per model)
4) roll a hotpatch to fix kernel selector heuristics later (post-mitigation)

Jamal R.: taking oncall. I'll execute step 1 and 2 now. Handoff ETA 5m. Night oncall: Jamal R. (Isha out)

Jamal R.: running admin change to disable continuous batching for pool=prod-heavy-1
```bash
curl -X POST "https://console.internal/api/v1/pools/prod-heavy-1/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": false, "batch_max_tokens": 128}'
```

Jamal R.: applied. Confirming via runtime API...

deploy-bot: CONFIG UPDATE applied to prod-heavy-1 (change_id=cfg-2026-11). Rolling to 3 nodes.

Alex M.: monitoring. Metrics starting to look better on node-7 and node-9, eviction rate down ~70% on those after change. Latency tail still elevated for a short window.

Elaine S.: next: forcing kernel fallback for the most affected model group (gptx-chat-long). Patch command:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap kernel-selector --type merge -p '{"data":{"gptx-chat-long":"force_fp16"}}'
```

deploy-bot: Kernel selection patch queued; will rollout to 2/3 nodes now to avoid correlated restart.

Maria P.: any quick customer comms? We should notify the customers showing errors/latency spikes.

Alex M.: I'll draft a short note for CS: "We're investigating increased latency for long-context chat routes; mitigation in progress; no data loss; next update in 30m."

Jamal R.: real-time numbers: KV_TOTAL_BYTES cluster went 7.8GB -> 2.1GB on affected nodes after continuous_batching=false + kernel fallback. Paging events dropped to baseline.

SRE Lead: good mitigation. Next steps for post-incident: capture kernel selector inputs, reproduce expansion factor in staging, add a canary to quant kernels that measures per-kv size inflation, and update rollout gating. Also add a temporary admission-control to throttle large-prefix bursts.

Elaine S.: note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis = awq-int8-v2 kernel selection combined with continuous batching kept oversized KV entries resident; padding/alignment + metadata per entry caused ~3-4x footprint vs prior path. That change didn't get a runtime canary for kv footprint.

Jamal R.: handing off to SRE for next 12h monitoring. My shift ends in 20m, but I'm available for questions. Handoff checklist uploaded: https://docs.internal/incidents/INC-3789/hand-off

Alex M.: thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with postmortem plan and CVE-like notes for customers if we decide to recommend specific quant paths. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — INC-3789 status=mitigated; mitigation_time=2481123310; responder=@Jamal R.; severity=sev2

Jamal R.: final note — applied a short-term hotpatch to kernel-selector heuristics to prefer older int8 when estimated_kv_bytes > 2GB. We'll revert after proper rollout.

Alex M.: closing loop: no customer data exposures, main impact was increased latency & partial paging; root follow-up actions assigned in the postmortem doc. We'll schedule a quant-path gating RFC next sprint.
